# Local YAML compatibility adapter

This is application-owned compatibility code, not a published serde_yaml release
or a patched copy of its deprecated implementation. The local version
`0.9.34+typsmthng-compat.1` declares the 0.9 API contract required by Typst 0.15.1
and Hayagriva 0.10.1. `publish = false` prevents publishing it as upstream.

Its only Rust implementation is `pub use yaml_serde::*;`. The dependency is the
unaltered crates.io release `yaml_serde 0.10.7`, backed by `libyaml-rs 0.3.0`.
Cargo.lock records both registry checksums. Neither upstream implementation is
vendored here. Typst, Hayagriva, and tests resolve the same public Error, Value,
Mapping, Serializer, Deserializer, and helper functions. This avoids a compiler
fork and the error-type mismatch from migrating one consumer alone.

The YAML organization documents package renaming as its migration path:
https://github.com/yaml/yaml-serde#migrating-from-serde_yaml
This adapter makes that migration available to transitive dependencies whose
manifests still require the old package name and API version. The local adapter
will need removal when compatible Typst and Hayagriva releases migrate upstream.

## Maintenance and limits

- https://github.com/yaml/yaml-serde declares an actively maintained official YAML
  organization fork. Registry owners identify Ingy döt Net. Release 0.10.7 was
  published on 2026-08-18 and fixes the source chain for IO errors. Its scheduled
  CI was passing on 2026-10-20.
- https://github.com/yaml/libyaml-rs declares YAML organization responsibility for
  the archived unsafe-libyaml fork. It is unarchived, owned by the same publisher,
  and released 0.3.0 on 2026-03-11. No later release or repository commit was found
  as of 2026-10-21. Its parser/scanner/emitter/API files are byte-identical to
  unsafe-libyaml 0.2.11. This candidate changes stewardship and the dependency
  implementation selected by Cargo. It does not claim rewritten parser algorithms
  or removal of unsafe Rust.
- https://yaml.com/projects/yaml-serde/ names the responsible maintainer and
  security reporting contact. This is the maintainer's commitment, not independent
  proof of audits or of memory safety.
- https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0449.html is an unmaintained notice
  about the archived unsafe-libyaml package, with no patched version. Its guidance
  suggests safe Rust parsers. It does not endorse this fork. Retaining the unsafe
  algorithm is an explicit limitation, separate from whether maintenance-only
  remediation is accepted.

MIT and Apache-2.0 license texts are retained from the yaml_serde 0.10.7 registry
archive for redistribution. libyaml-rs is MIT-licensed. There are no advisory
ignores. No YAML mode is configured differently, no syntax is rewritten, and no
format or feature is disabled. The maintained backend fixes Error::source for IO
errors; it preserves the tested Display, Debug, and location fields.

## Compatibility evidence

`native/gtk/tests/fixtures/yaml-legacy-behavior.json` was generated by the same
behavior-report function in `yaml_compatibility.rs`, compiled in a separate
scratch crate with unmodified registry serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated. The fixture
records 33 inputs through string/slice/reader/stream APIs, YAML Value and JSON
Value conversion, exact serialized text, explicit merge application, error
Display/Debug/index/line/column, invalid UTF-8, tagged enums, and float encoding.
The integration test compares the maintained chain to those frozen results.
Additional tests compile actual YAML data, serialization, YAML bibliography,
and malformed files through the preview compiler and compare SVG output and
all diagnostic fields with the unchanged Typst 0.15.1 CLI; PDF compilation is
also exercised. Existing syntax and packdump compatibility tests remain active.

Typst 0.15.1 accepts raw bytes through `yaml(bytes(...))`; `yaml.decode` is absent
in that upstream version. Both preview and CLI must preserve its existing
unknown-field diagnostic rather than introducing a new public API here.

The libyaml-rs archive records VCS SHA
`66d8ae3d348b328ef2159e3dc0bc53f1deb4c3a2`, which the official GitHub API
cannot resolve. Its archive checksum is verified against the registry, and every
published Rust source/test file, original manifest, README, and MIT license was
also compared byte for byte with the official release commit
`e95b9a3e83bfb00728162c82e61e393c393929d1`. All matched. The archive's original
VCS metadata is recorded in the candidate provenance report without alteration.
